1#main: The laws of a firstborn at this time. In it are 2 seifim. A firstborn at this time has no permit except through a blemish; and even if the owners or the kohen wish to put it in a pen until it dies by itself, they are not permitted—rather the kohen must raise it until a blemish befalls it.
2#main: Even when a blemish befalls it openly and is recognizable to all, such as if its hand or foot was cut off and the like—it is not permitted to slaughter it except according to an expert who instructs him that it is a blemish fit to be slaughtered for; and if there is no expert sage, it is permitted according to three members of the community—meaning, somewhat learned men who are not so expert. And nowadays, when there are no experts, it is not slaughtered according to three members of the community except for clear blemishes, such as if its eye was blinded, its hand cut off, and the like. And a split ear is a clear blemish where the split is recognizable and visible to the eyes that it is more than the circumference of a fingernail. And how is a split ear? When it was damaged through deficiency from the cartilage and not the skin on the lip of the ear—whether it was damaged by human action or by heaven. {Rama: If the tail was cut above the joint, it is a blemish (Piskei Maharai siman 246). And the author of the Tur enumerated several more blemishes for which they slaughter at this time; and the rabbi who composed this book followed the Rambam's words—and it appears to me that one who relies on the Tur's words, built on the Rosh's view, does not lose.}
